builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How Far Can the Gemma 4 Speech Encoder Go Without Changing Its Weights? Saudi and Gulf Arabic Speech Recognition with a Frozen and an Adapter-Augmented Encoder
summary: The method replaces full fine-tuning of a speech foundation model (or reliance on a commercial ASR API) with a frozen pretrained encoder plus a small trainable CTC or hybrid CTC/attention reader and optional low-rank adapters, targeting Arabic dialect ASR. It costs training and validation effort on domain data (around 25.7M to 44.6M trainable parameters), still trails the commercial baseline in WER on long-form speech, and adds pipeline complexity in layer mixing and joint decoding. It can fail on domains far from the Saudi/Gulf data used, and the paper itself warns that human-corrected machine drafts bias evaluation toward the drafting system.
rationale: For a team with one GPU and a limited budget, freezing a 305M encoder and training small readers is feasible infrastructure-wise, but the dialect-specific and evaluation-bias caveats require workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Frozen speech encoder with lightweight CTC/adapter readers for ASR

claims.statement: The method replaces full fine-tuning of a speech foundation model (or reliance on a commercial ASR API) with a frozen pretrained encoder plus a small trainable CTC or hybrid CTC/attention reader and optional low-rank adapters, targeting Arabic dialect ASR. It costs training and validation effort on domain data (around 25.7M to 44.6M trainable parameters), still trails the commercial baseline in WER on long-form speech, and adds pipeline complexity in layer mixing and joint decoding. It can fail on domains far from the Saudi/Gulf data used, and the paper itself warns that human-corrected machine drafts bias evaluation toward the drafting system.

Frozen 305M encoder system runs 3.4x faster than Cohere Transcribe Arabic (2.07B) on CPU with greedy decoding, and the adapted system reaches 139x real time on one GPU with an optimised joint decoder, while remaining statistically comparable in CER on five of six conditions.
